notes.meaning: Miriam and Aaron spoke out against Moses because he had married a Cushite woman. Miriam is named first, which suggests she took the lead in complaining against her brother. People often identify this woman as Zipporah from Midian, though some think Moses took a second wife from Cush or Ethiopia. In either case, the family complaint served as an excuse to challenge Moses' position.

Aaron and Miriam claimed equal authority with Moses. They argued that because God had also given them the gift of prophecy, Moses had no right to lead alone. God heard their proud words and the challenge to His chosen leader.

Moses is described as more meek, or humble, than anyone else on the earth. He did not lose his temper or try to defend his own honor against his brother and sister. Because Moses refused to fight back, God Himself stepped in to defend him.

The Lord called Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to come at once to the Tent of Meeting, the sacred tent where God met with His people. God acted quickly to stop this family rebellion before it could spread through the camp. All three went out immediately to face the Lord.

The Lord came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the Tent. He called Aaron and Miriam to step forward away from Moses. Keeping them outside the doorway was a clear sign that God was displeased with them.

The Lord explained how He usually speaks to a prophet. He makes Himself known to prophets through visions or dreams, which can be indirect and hard to understand. Not every messenger receives God's word in the same way.

God declared that Moses was not like ordinary prophets. Moses was placed over all God's house, meaning the whole nation of Israel, and was completely faithful in his work. He did everything God asked of him without seeking personal gain.

God spoke with Moses directly and plainly, like two friends speaking face to face, rather than in riddles. Moses was even allowed to see a visible sign of God's glorious presence. The Lord asked Aaron and Miriam why they were bold enough to speak against such a trusted servant.

The Lord's anger burned against Aaron and Miriam for their rebellion. After delivering His rebuke, He departed from them without waiting for their reply. The removal of God's presence was an unmistakable sign of His deep displeasure.

When the cloud lifted from the Tent, Miriam was suddenly covered with leprosy, turning her skin white as snow. Aaron turned and saw the terrible disease on his sister. Miriam was struck because she led the rebellion, while Aaron was spared so the holy priesthood would not be disgraced.

Aaron immediately humbled himself and addressed Moses with deep respect as 'my lord.' He confessed that they had acted foolishly and sinned against God and Moses. He begged his younger brother not to hold the punishment of their sin against them.

Aaron pleaded for Miriam not to be left like a stillborn baby whose flesh is already rotting away. Severe leprosy caused living body tissue to decay and waste away. Aaron could not bear to see his sister suffer this living death.
Moses showed his true humility by crying out to God to heal his sister right away. He held no grudge against Miriam for her insults. Instead, he immediately pleaded for mercy on her behalf.

The Lord heard Moses' prayer, but He decreed that Miriam must still bear public shame for seven days. If a father showed disgust by spitting in a daughter's face, she would be separated in shame for a full week. Miriam had to follow the standard rule for skin disease by staying outside the camp for seven days before returning clean.

Miriam was shut outside the camp for seven days as the Lord commanded. The entire camp waited and did not travel until she was brought back inside. This showed respect for her role as a leader while also reminding everyone of the serious cost of rebellion.

After Miriam rejoined the people, the camp packed up and moved on from Hazeroth. They set up their next camp in the Wilderness of Paran. This brought Israel near Kadesh, right at the southern border of the Promised Land.
